title: Health, Psychology, and Resilience
summary: Mental health, stress, protective factors, prevention, access to care, and social resilience.
whyItMatters: Health is shaped by biological, psychological, social, and institutional factors, so prevention and support require more than individual willpower.

mentalModel.title: Risk and protection interact
mentalModel.content: Stressors raise strain while relationships, resources, routines, autonomy, and professional support can buffer their effects.

mentalModel.title: Resilience is not invulnerability
mentalModel.content: Resilience describes adaptation with available support, not an obligation to endure harmful conditions.

ruleBlocks.title: Differentiate stress processes
ruleBlocks.content: Distinguish demands, appraisal, short-term reactions, chronic strain, coping, and recovery.

ruleBlocks.title: Use levels of prevention
ruleBlocks.content: Compare universal prevention, early intervention for risk groups, and treatment or relapse prevention.

ruleBlocks.title: Analyze barriers to care
ruleBlocks.content: Include cost, waiting times, language, stigma, location, trust, and continuity.

examples.de: Dauerhafte Überlastung kann die Erholung beeinträchtigen, selbst wenn einzelne Stressphasen gut bewältigt werden.
examples.en: Persistent overload can impair recovery even when individual periods of stress are managed well.

examples.de: Soziale Unterstützung wirkt häufig als Schutzfaktor, ersetzt aber keine professionelle Behandlung.
examples.en: Social support often acts as a protective factor but does not replace professional treatment.

examples.de: Prävention ist wirksamer, wenn auch belastende Arbeits- und Lebensbedingungen verändert werden.
examples.en: Prevention is more effective when stressful working and living conditions are also changed.

commonMistakes.wrong: Explain mental health only through personal attitude.
commonMistakes.correct: Include social conditions, resources, health factors, and access to support.
Describe observed experiences unless a qualified diagnosis is relevant.
commonMistakes.reason: Clinical terms have specific meanings and consequences.

comparisons.summary: Causal linking helps explain interacting stressors, protective factors, and outcomes.
The communication lesson supports respectful conversations without diagnosing or taking over.
